document.title: Phase 8: EXI
document.p: Goal: all of Efficient XML Interchange 1.0 (Second Edition, W3C Recommendation 2014) and Canonical EXI (W3C Recommendation 2018) in sxml, read and written through the tree builder and the serializer, shipped in release 0.3.0. A packet starts when every packet in its "After" list is committed. Phase 8 must not regress the counts of Phases 2 to 7.

item.p: Headers first. Packet 8.2 writes every public declaration of the phase; later packets change no header in include/sxml/, and a need for one is a proposal.
The ratchet.tests/exi/passing.txt lists the golden cases that pass. The exi/golden test fails when one of them fails; a packet adds the cases it makes pass, and removes none.

The gate script.tools/exi/check-packet.sh runs what a packet must pass: the debug preset with sanitizers, the EXI unit tests and the ratchet, clang-tidy on the changed files, the call-cycle check, and no change under include/sxml/.

section.title: Packets
section.p: Each packet gives what it implements, what it owns, what it needs first ("After") and when it is done.

item.p: Every golden case of tests/exi/manifest.tsv that EXIficient accepts passes: decoded as EXIficient decodes it, and encoded to the same bytes (compression decoded instead), and every case EXIficient refuses is refused.
The counts of Phases 2 to 7 have not dropped, and sxml.wasm is within its budget.
Each decoder entry point (the stream, DEFLATE, the options document) has a fuzz target, run briefly here and fully on the owner's machine.
The command, the host shim and the JavaScript package reach the codecs, each with tests, and the book has an EXI page.
